Subject: Eval smoothing proposal + exceptions workflow

Hi team,

Ahead of next week’s cross-team calibration I pulled together a short proposal for a smoothing band approach and an exceptions workflow we can use when managers disagree by >1 full point. The goal is to reduce anchoring-driven outliers while making the appeals path auditable for HR and exec review.

Summary (attached):
- Smoothing band: if a manager’s distribution shows >15% in the top bucket, apply a +/– 0.25 smoothing to bring closer to the cohort median for discussion only (not final).
- Exceptions: documented exception form (template attached) that managers submit to People Ops for any proposed >1 point deviation; requires direct manager + skip-level sign-off.
- Timing: run the calibration meeting on Wed 11/11; finalize escalations by Fri 11/13.

Attachments: calibration_matrix_Q4.xlsx (matrix + guidance), team_ratings_snapshot.pdf (raw manager inputs), exceptions_log_TEMPLATE.docx

Please review and reply with:
1) Any operational concerns (esp. how this will affect comp planning timelines).
2) If you have specific names that will need pre-clearing for exceptions.

Also looping in Karen and Luca because a couple of our customers asked about how we handle rating exceptions and we’d like to have consistent talking points.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — read the doc. Two quick flagged items:

1) Anchoring risk: smoothing is fine as a discussion aid, but if we show managers the cohort median before they submit final ratings we risk nudging them. Recommend we present medians during calibration only (not as a prefill).

2) Timing: CompOps needs final numbers by 11/18 to model budgets. If we push escalations to 11/13 that’s tight but doable; want explicit SLA that HR will review exception forms within 48 hours of submission.

Operational asks from my side:
- Can we add a short field in the exception template: "Business-critical justification" so we can prioritize reviews?
- Please confirm whether exceptions trigger any changes to bonus targets or just rating labels (we need to know for compensation messaging).

I'll have two managers (Ben Carter, Markus Klein) flagged for potential exceptions — sending heads-up offline.

-laura

Appreciate the draft, Rishi. I ran a quick simulation against last year’s distributions and attached a snapshot. A few notes:

- The +/–0.25 smoothing reduces apparent top-heavy skew in most teams without changing headcount for calibration buckets. It does, however, compress the "needs coaching" tail which may obscure real performance issues — recommend we exclude ICs on PIPs from smoothing.
- Exceptions: concur with Laura on SLA. Also suggest a triage queue: People Ops + Manager Relations review first, then escalate to Monica for any promotion/comp-impact exceptions.
- Communication: recommend an internal FAQ doc for managers summarizing the appeals path and examples. I can draft the FAQ if we agree on mechanics.

Proposed edits: add the FAQ link (draft) and a short checkbox in the template to indicate whether the exception affects comp/level. See attached: team_ratings_snapshot.pdf (with simulation overlay).

If folks are okay, I can present an executive summary (5 slides) at the calibration meeting and run the triage workflow for the first 48 hours post-meeting.
